title: GTM opportunity maps — ops-first verticals (fintech, health, legal, enterprise SaaS, gov)
content:
Purpose and scope:
- Quick working brief to align message hooks and pilot asks for ops-focused buyers across 5 verticals: fintech, healthcare, legal, enterprise SaaS, gov/defense.
- Emphasis: inference economics, SLAs/availability, compliant private deployment options, and predictable upgrade/rollout paths.
- Outcome: one short pilot template per vertical + 3 headline messages for landing pages and SDR outreach.

Audience & buyer personas (ops-first lens):
- Platform/infra leads (SRE, infra eng): care about latency SLOs, deterministic performance, rollout safety, observability.
- ML infra/product (ML engineers): model compatibility, model lifecycle, quantization tradeoffs, reproducibility of evals.
- Security/compliance (CISO, GRC): private deployment, KMS/HSM, audit logs, data residency.
- Product/business buyer (Head of Product, CTO): cost per 1k predictions, reliability in peak usage, vendor lock-in risk.

High-level GTM proposition (ops-first):
- Headline: "Predictable inference. Measurable economics. Zero-surprise rollouts."
- Subheads to test: "Move from experimental to production with predictable LLM costs and SLOs" / "Run inference where your data and compliance needs live — with SLA-backed routing"

Vertical-specific notes (short pilots + messaging hooks):
1) Fintech — payments/risk scoring / customer service assistants
- Primary pain: spikes during market events, p99 tail latency causing timeouts, auditability for model decisions.
- Message pillars: deterministic latency, explainable reranking, audit trail + model versioning for compliance.
- Pilot ask (4–6 weeks): integrate Redwood Dedicated with a risk-scoring endpoint, synthetic load tests (peak 3x traffic), and 5 sample queries traced for decision lineage.
- Success metrics: p99 latency < 300ms, SLA error-rate < 0.1%, end-to-end cost per 1k tokens reduced by >=25% vs current.
- Competitors to call out: large managed endpoint players that lack dedicated private routing or transparent per-token economics.
- Objections likely: "We can't risk model drift affecting regulatory reporting" -> Response: model pinning + canary rollouts + eval regression alerts.

2) Healthcare — clinical summarization, prior auth helpers
- Primary pain: PHI handling, air-gapped/on-prem requirements, strict audit trails.
- Message pillars: private deployment, KMS integrations, retention and redaction controls, certified logging for audits.
- Pilot ask: on-prem pilot for a subset of clinical summarization pipelines, HIPAA DPA + security review, ingest sample de-identified data for accuracy checks.
- Success metrics: compliance checklist signoff, accuracy delta vs baseline < 2% (clinically acceptable), throughput targets met (XX doc/min).
- Competitors: niche healthcare ML shops and DIY infra; our angle is prebuilt compliance controls + inference economics.

3) Legal — contract analytics and discovery assistants
- Primary pain: privacy, chain of custody, model hallucinations on legal facts.
- Message pillars: auditable prompts/outputs, freeze-frame evidence snapshots, model variants optimized for precision (not verbosity).
- Pilot ask: integrate Redwood Private with existing discovery pipeline for a focused use-case (contract clause extraction), measure precision/recall on annotated set.
- Success metrics: precision > 92% on clause extraction, audit log completeness, rollout plan to prod in 8 weeks.

4) Enterprise SaaS — embedded copilots, support automation
- Primary pain: cost at scale (many low-value queries), latency for in-app experiences, multi-tenant isolation.
- Message pillars: intelligent batching/caching suggestions, tenant-level quota and cost breakdowns, canary rollout + fallback to smaller models to control cost.
- Pilot ask: connect one high-traffic tenant flow to Redwood Hosted with caching and autoscaling rules; measure cost per end-user action and perceived latency.
- Success metrics: cost per active user down 30% in flow, 95th percentile latency <= 200ms for in-app calls.

5) Gov / defense — classified data patterns, long-term support
- Primary pain: air-gapped deployments, long procurement cycles, strict accreditation, local hosting.
- Message pillars: private control plane for VPC/on-prem, support for long-term hardened deployments, partner-certified installers.
- Pilot ask: compliance readout + whitepaper for STIG/FISMA mapping, small on-prem PoC with secure KMS, measured uptime targets.
- Success metrics: architecture approved by security review board, demonstrable isolated network deployment in lab, response playbook for incident drills.

Cross-vertical competitive differentiators to emphasize:
- Unified experience across hosted, dedicated, private: "same API, same telemetry, different trust boundaries"
- Observable economics: token-level cost transparency + recommendations (quantization, batching) tied to predicted savings
- Rollout safety primitives: model pinning, canaries, A/B, automatic fallback to compatible variants when capacity is constrained
- Production-first runtime optimizations that reduce p99 latency without sacrificing throughput

One-liners and email subject tests (ops tuned):
- Subject: "Cut inference cost spikes by 25% — pilot for your infra team?"
- Subject: "Private LLM pilot: 4 weeks to audit-ready inference"
- Quick line: "We help infra teams make LLMs predictable — latency SLOs, clear economics, no surprises in rollouts."

Pilot template (standardized):
- Duration: 4–6 weeks
- Kickoff: security & architecture sync (week 0)
- Phase 1: ingest & small-scale model validation (week 1–2)
- Phase 2: load tests, canary or isolated tenant rollout (week 3–4)
- Phase 3: ops handoff & playbooks (week 5–6)
- Deliverables: runbook, cost projection, performance report, recommended rollout policy

Metrics & dashboard must-haves for closing deals:
- p50/p95/p99 latency per route
- cost per 1k tokens (baseline vs optimized)
- cache hit rate and effective tokens saved
- model-regression alerts tied to a prompt-set (quality score)
- audit log completeness (per model/prompt)

Field notes / unknowns / to validate with sales-engineering:
- How often do fintech buyers require model explainability beyond audit trails? (ask AE leads)
- For healthcare, what is minimum requirements list for an internal security review? Static doc please.
- Do legal buyers prefer precision-focused short-answer models or retrieval-augmented longforms?
- Enterprise SaaS buyers will want tenant-level billing. Confirm feasibility for next quarter billing product.
- Gov/defense: procurement timeline assumptions — are we offering a pre-approved vendor list?

Next steps (short-run):
- Align with solutions engineering on 3 pilot kits (fintech, healthcare, enterprise SaaS). Jonah to own fintech kit.
- Create one-pager collateral (Priya) and a 1-slide pilot checklist per vertical.
- Prepare secure architecture template for healthcare and gov (Liam + infra).
- Sales: test 4 subject lines in SDR outbound this quarter; report CTR and SQL conversion.

Notes to self / rough ideas:
- Consider a small "ops ROI calculator" (spreadsheet) that takes avg tokens per request, traffic profile, and shows cost delta with batching/quantization. Useful for RFC with finance buyers.
- Draft an internal objection playbook mapping security concerns to features (private + KMS + logs + sev support).
